 Order

This first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C/483 of BNSS,
2023 for grant of regular bail in relation to FIR No.648/2023 dated 14.11.2023 registered at Police Station Govindpura District Bhopal (M.P.) for commission of offence under Sections 363,
365,376,376(2)(n) of IPC and Section 3, 4(2),5(L)/ 6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

Applicant is in detention since 27.04.2024.
3.
As per the prosecution story, on 04.03.2023, prosecutrix mother lodged report about missing of her 15 years old daughter since intervening night of 3-4/11/2023.
When despite search she could not be traced, F.I.R was registered.
Prosecutrix was recovered on 27.04.2024 from the possession of the present applicant.
After investigation, charge sheet has already been filed.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.

It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:21371 2 MCRC-13951-2025 submitted that prosecutrix was consenting party.
She was above 18 years of age and she on her own had gone with the applicant.
It is contended that prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial Court and in cross examination she has stated that she had gone on her own with Rahul and has no birth certificate.
Therefore, it is prayed that present applicant may be released on bail.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer for the State has opposed grant of bail and has submitted that at the time of commission of offence prosecutrix was 15 years old and DNA report is positive.
It is submitted that in ossification test too her age has been assessed to be 15-1/2 years.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may not be released on bail.
6. Prosecutrix has already been examined before the trial court and she has supported the prosecution story.
As far as age of the prosecutrix is concerned, in ossification test her age has been determined to be 15-1/2 years.
Minor's consent is immaterial and inconsequential.

Therefore,
having taken into consideration the material on record, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail.
Consequently, this first bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C/483 of BNSS filed on behalf of the applicant is dismissed.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Rahul Sarwan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106481382/
